cards.text: This is a psalm of David, king of Israel, written for the choirmaster to the tune of "The Doe of the Dawn." Pretty name for a tune, right? Then David opens his mouth: "My God, my God, why have You forsaken me?"

cards.question: In his opening cry, David says God feels so far away. So far from doing what for him?

cards.text: Friend, you might know that line. Jesus cried it out from the cross (Matthew 27:46).

cards.question: True or false: David says he cries out to God by day and by night, and God answers him right away.

cards.text: Then David says, "Yet You are holy, enthroned on the praises of Israel." And he remembers Israel's fathers, the ones who trusted God.

cards.question: When Israel's fathers trusted God, He ___ them.

cards.text: Then David says, "But I am a worm and not a man, scorned by men and despised by the people." Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer where the dead batteries I lived with looked down on ME.

cards.question: The people who see David sneer that since he trusts in the LORD, the LORD should ___ him.

cards.text: But David turns back to God with another "Yet." "Yet You brought me forth from the womb; You made me secure at my mother’s breast."

cards.question: True or false: David says God has been his God only since he became king.
David pleads with God, "Be not far from me." What reason does he give?

answers.text: Trouble is near and no one can help
He wants to see a sign from heaven
His enemies have all run away

cards.text: Now David paints his enemies as wild animals. Strong bulls of Bashan encircle him, and they open their jaws like lions that roar and maul.

cards.question: David says he is poured out like water and his heart melts like wax. What is he describing?

cards.text: His strength is dried up like a potsherd, and his tongue sticks to the roof of his mouth. Then he tells God, "You lay me in the dust of death."
And it gets darker. Dogs surround him, a band of evil men encircles him, and "they have pierced my hands and feet."

cards.question: True or false: David says he is so worn down that he can count all his bones.
The men around David stare and gloat. What do they do with his clothing?

cards.text: Hold on, friend. John says the soldiers at Jesus' cross divided His clothes and cast lots, to fulfill this very Scripture (John 19:23–24).
Then David calls out one more time. "But You, O LORD, be not far off; O my Strength, come quickly to help me."

cards.question: David begs God to deliver him from the sword and from the power of wild dogs. What is he asking God to save?

cards.text: "Save me from the mouth of the lion," David prays. Then, right in the middle of that line, at the horns of the wild oxen, something changes.

cards.question: At the horns of the wild oxen, what does David suddenly say God has done?

cards.text: Back at the start, David said, "but You do not answer." Now it's "You have answered me!" and friend, the whole psalm just turned around.

cards.question: Now that God has answered, David says he will ___ God's name to his brothers.
True or false: David calls only the priests to praise the LORD.

cards.text: David calls everyone who fears the LORD, all of Jacob's descendants, to praise Him. And he tells them why.

cards.question: David gives Israel a reason to praise the LORD. What has the LORD done for the afflicted one?

cards.text: His praise resounds in the great assembly, and he'll fulfill his vows before those who fear God. From "I am a worm" to praise ringing through the great assembly? Friend, THAT is a comeback.

cards.question: David says the ___ will eat and be satisfied.

cards.text: Then the picture gets BIG. All the ends of the earth will remember and turn to the LORD, and all the families of the nations will bow down before Him.

cards.question: True or false: David says the nations will bow before the LORD because He rules over them.
True or false: David says the rich of the earth are left out of the worship.

cards.text: Even all who go down to the dust will kneel before Him, even those unable to preserve their lives.

cards.question: As the psalm ends, how far will the news about the LORD reach?

cards.text: They will proclaim His righteousness "to a people yet unborn—all that He has done." A psalm that started in the dark ends on all that God has done.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 11 quotes "Be not far from me.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 18 has a dash outside a quotation: "Hold on, friend. John says the soldiers at Jesus' cross divided His clothes and cast lots, to fulfill this very Scripture (John 19:23–24)."

rule.text: No em dashes or en dashes to make a sentence longer.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 5 quotes "but You do not answer.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: "Pretty name for a tune, right?" is Papa Dorin's only personality beat on the opening card, and it reads like a nice dad being pleasant rather than a real laugh.

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: This story card tells nothing new from Psalm 22. It only connects verse 1 to Jesus' cry from the cross (Matthew 27:46). Outside facts are allowed when they help, but every story card is also supposed to move the baker forward through the passage.
findings.question: Can a story card be given entirely to a New Testament fulfillment or quotation of the verse just told (such as Matthew 27:46 for Psalm 22:1), or must that connection ride along on a card that also moves the passage forward?

findings.problem: The joke invents a new backstory detail: the dead batteries in the drawer looked down on Papa Dorin. The backstory says the drawer's residents 'were all in it together,' and joke inventions are limited to small moments around his bakery.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: The question says the mockers want the LORD to rescue David 'since he trusts in the LORD.' In Psalm 22:8 the 'since' belongs to 'He delights in him,' not to his trusting. This changes how the text connects its two ideas.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The statement adds a reason the text doesn't give. It says David is 'so worn down that' he can count all his bones. Psalm 22:17 only says 'I can count all my bones.'

rule.text: Reasons: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: The setup inside the question ('The men around David stare and gloat') rules out the wrong answer 'Hand it back to him.'

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Like stop 1 card 3, this story card tells nothing new from Psalm 22. It only gives John 19:23–24's fulfillment of verse 18.
findings.question: Can a story card be given entirely to a New Testament fulfillment of the verse just told (such as John 19:23–24 for Psalm 22:18), or must that connection ride along on a card that also moves the passage forward?

findings.problem: Story card 3 says 'something changes' at the horns of the wild oxen. That rules out both wrong answers ('Left him alone' and 'Turned away from him'), since both describe no change from the lament.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'Left him alone' is close to what David says in Psalm 22:1 ('why have You forsaken me?'), so it isn't false everywhere in the passage. The two wrong answers also mean nearly the same thing as each other.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: This card only looks back, contrasting verse 2 with verse 21, which was already told on card 3 and asked on card 4. It adds nothing new and doesn't move the passage forward.
This story card has three sentences. Only the opening card may go past two.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Story card 12 already says 'all the ends of the earth' and 'all the families of the nations' will turn to the LORD. That rules out 'Only to David's family' and 'Only to Jerusalem.' Both wrong answers also share the 'Only' framing, which makes the right answer stand out.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.
